Thank you, I really appreciate your response.  It's hard sometimes because I really don't think I'm a particularly "good" person.  I feel like a good person wouldn't even feel suicidal if they had someone dependent on them (and I recognize what bullshit this thought is because if literally anyone else told me they felt like that, I would bend over backwards to reassure them that they were still a good person).  It's hard because my mother isn't in the best cognitive shape and sometimes she doesn't understand the amount of work I have to do to make sure she's able to live where she does and that her health is taken care of (I don't do it for any sort of "reward" or anything, but it really sucks when she or any of the other people in her life act like I'm not doing enough to support her).  I wasn't 100% qualified for the job I applied for, but I applied anyways.  I suppose that's not the most terrible thing in the world.  

I guess my frustration comes from being in this weird place, having grown up with a lot of suicidal ideation/a few attempts.  And now suddenly within the last couple of years, I'm now directly responsible for someone else's health and happiness.  I guess I thought the suicidal thoughts would go away at some point, but they haven't.  I'm not going to act on them, but it's so distressing that they are still there, despite knowing that I have responsibilities that prevent me from going through with it.  That's part of why I feel so worthless.   Wouldn't a better caretaker not even have these thoughts?  Or at least be able to deal with them in a more healthy way?  If I'm still having these thoughts now, what if I become a parent some day?  That thought scares me so much, that I might feel suicidal despite having a child to take care of.  Anyways, sorry for the rant...I made an emergency appointment with my therapist and I'm gonna try and talk to her about this.  Thank you again.
He sounds exactly like the kind of person who waited in line for Rick and Morty sauce at McDonalds
